passage:
A student visited a mountain village and saw the Milky Way for the first time. Back in the city, the night sky showed only a few stars.
Her science teacher explained light pollution. Streetlights, signs, and buildings send light upward, making the sky too bright to see many stars.
The class studied safer lighting designs that point downward. They also learned that darkness matters for birds, insects, and sleep.
The student wrote an essay called "The Stars We Hide."
She did not want the city to become dark and unsafe. She wanted people to use light more wisely. The stars were not gone. The city had simply covered them.
